findings.key_quote: Our provision for income taxes in 2025 increased $17.17 billion or 207% compared to 2024, primarily due to an increase in the effective tax rate. Our effective tax rate in 2025 increased compared to 2024, mostly due to the effects of OBBBA.
findings.justification: This evidence from the 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2025 (EXACT_MATCH period) directly states that Meta's effective tax rate increased in 2025 compared to 2024, and that this increase was mostly due to the effects of OBBBA (One Big Beautiful Bill Act), which is U.S. tax law. This entails the assertion that the effective tax rate increased mainly because of a one-time charge related to U.S. tax law changes.

findings.key_quote: we recorded a $15.93 billion charge in the third quarter of 2025, of which $14.03 billion was a valuation allowance against our U.S. federal deferred tax assets as of the enactment date of OBBBA
findings.justification: This evidence from the 10-K provides the specific one-time charge amount ($15.93 billion) related to OBBBA (U.S. tax law changes) that was recorded in 2025. While the period_status is MISMATCH (3M vs 12M), the passage explicitly discusses the full year 2025 impact, stating 'Our provision for income taxes in 2025 increased $17.17 billion or 207% compared to 2024, primarily due to an increase in the effective tax rate. Our effective tax rate in 2025 increased compared to 2024, mostly due to the effects of OBBBA.' This establishes the causal link between the one-time charge and the effective tax rate increase for the full year.

findings.key_quote: we recorded a $15.93 billion one-time charge related to the implementation as of the enactment date of OBBBA
findings.justification: This evidence from the 10-Q for nine months ended September 30, 2025 (MISMATCH period) describes the one-time charge related to OBBBA and states that provision for income taxes increased mostly due to increases in effective tax rate. However, this covers only 9 months of 2025, not the full year, so it does not decide whether this was the main cause for the full year 2025.

findings.key_quote: Our effective tax rate increased in the three and nine months ended September 30, 2025 compared to the same periods in 2024, mostly due to the implementation of OBBBA
findings.justification: This evidence from the 10-Q confirms that the effective tax rate increased in the nine months ended September 30, 2025 mostly due to OBBBA implementation. However, the period is 9 months (MISMATCH), not the full year 2025, so it does not decide the claim about the full year.

findings.key_quote: Effective tax rate was 87% for the three months ended September 30, 2025. This includes a one-time income tax charge of $15.93 billion accrued in the third quarter of 2025
findings.justification: This evidence provides the effective tax rate for Q3 2025 (87%) and mentions the one-time charge, but this is for three months only (MISMATCH period), not the full year 2025, so it does not decide the annual claim.

findings.key_quote: Our effective tax rate was flat in the three months ended June 30, 2025 compared to the same period in 2024. Our effective tax rate decreased in the six months ended June 30, 2025 compared to the same period in 2024
findings.justification: This evidence from the 10-Q for periods ended June 30, 2025 (MISMATCH) shows that the effective tax rate was flat or decreased in the first half of 2025, which is context about a different period but does not decide what happened for the full year 2025.

findings.key_quote: Absent any changes to our tax landscape, we expect our effective tax rate for the full year 2026 to be in the range of 13-16%.
findings.justification: This evidence is forward-looking, discussing expectations for 2026, not what happened in 2025. It does not decide the claim about 2025 results.
